walkthroughs.body_html: Carbon fibre and GRP are composites — strong fibres held by a resin matrix. They are light, stiff and corrosion-free, which is why they appear in racing bikes, boat hulls and aircraft parts.

Kevlar has fibres five times stronger than steel by weight. It is woven into bulletproof vests, motorcycle gloves and yacht ropes. Like all composites, its strength comes from fibre direction and bonding.

Comparing a steel and a carbon fibre frame: steel is cheap and easy to weld but heavier; carbon fibre is light and stiff but costly and hard to repair. A pro racer pays the premium for carbon fibre's weight saving.
